American Federal observation balloon Intrepid being inflated. Civil War Battle of Fair Oaks, Va., May 1862

Photo by Matthew Brady.

The Union Army Balloon Corps was a branch of the Union Army during the American Civil War. It was organized as a civilian operation, which employed a group of prominent American aeronauts and seven specially built, gas-filled balloons.

Each balloon was assigned 2 hydrogen gas generators. The Intrepid was a balloon (or aerostat) built for aerial reconnaissance purposes during the American Civil War. It was one of seven balloons constructed for the Balloon Corps and was one of the four larger balloons designed to make ascensions to higher elevations with a larger lift capacity for telegraph equipment and an operator.
